result.rationale: The diff shows `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` followed by `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal is always a non-empty string (at minimum ': '), so the `||` fallback is unreachable dead code, and when `err.data?.code` is undefined the toast renders 'undefined: ...'. Both consequences are directly verifiable from the added code in AddGuestsDialog.tsx.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the onError handler builds `message` as a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always produce a (truthy) string, even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined`, yielding e.g. `"undefined: ..."`. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback and can display an incorrect `undefined:` prefix instead of the intended generic message.
